content.title: About
content.content: Dessert dip is a sweet, creamy topping designed to accompany ice cream, fruit, pancakes and other desserts. It is usually made from cream, sugar and flavorings such as vanilla, caramel or berries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dessert dips are often used in restaurants to create visual contrast with the main dessert.
There are more than 30 flavor variations: chocolate, caramel, berry, nut and others.
In the United States, cheese‑based dips like cream‑cheese berry sauce are popular.
Traditional French "crème de fruit" is made from fresh fruit, sugar and lemon juice.
In Japan, a sweet rice‑paste dip called "mochi" is commonly served with desserts.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cream base provides calcium, which is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Some versions are fortified with vitamin D, helping the body absorb calcium.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Contains easily digestible sugars that can quickly replenish energy after physical activity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base can cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dip in small portions alongside a dessert, drizzling it over ice cream, pancakes, waffles or fresh fruit. It can also be used as a filling for cupcakes and rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dip refrigerated at 2 °C–4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 5–7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or changes color.
